lines.text: Many good teams use P on distance, carefully tuned. Here are two.
B-Line is a small, student-run path library. Speed is P times the distance left along the path.
It adds a push back toward the line, and a limit on how fast speed changes.
It gains many-point paths from an editor, with heading turning smoothly along the way.
It gives up moving goals, since the path is fixed once it starts. And its P must stay gentle.
Team twenty fifty-six, OP Robotics, uses P on distance with a speed cap.
To line up, they measure the scoring spot from the robot and move the end point to match.
It gains simplicity. It gives up the same choice: brake late, or creep in.
We tested simple copies of these rules, not their real robots.
Ours keeps the same position-based idea, plus one line: the stopping distance.
